title: Batch-aligned KV lease architecture and GPU pinning behavior
creator: Priya Singh
description: Implement and validate a lease-based KV cache coordination layer that aligns page residency with continuous batching windows and exposes deterministic GPU memory pinning behavior. This ticket covers: 1) defining lease semantics for batch boundaries to avoid unnecessary GPU page churn during high QPS; 2) integrating a pin/unpin protocol with the runtime's scheduler so pinned pages are excluded from preemption without blocking other tenants; 3) heuristics to choose per-request pin duration based on batch size and token horizon; and 4) instrumentation and benchmarks to measure end-to-end latency and GPU memory pressure under mixed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Lease API implemented: AcquireLease(page_id, duration_hint, batch_id) and Renew/Release semantics documented
Prefetch + pin path integrated with batching coordinator and default enabled for batch_size >= 8
Measured regression: tail P95 generation latency not worse than 5% relative to baseline when enabling lease pinning for internal perf harness
GPU resident set churn reduced: page eviction rate decreased by >= 30% for sustained continuous-batching traces collected from prod-sim
End-to-end tests and e2e perf job added to CI; at least two synthetic mixes (chatty short-turn + long context) included
Design doc and rollout checklist reviewed and approved by Runtime and Infra leads
technical_notes: Lease semantics: lease is advisory for eviction; eviction scorer subtracts active lease weight to avoid evicting recently used pages in active batches
Pinning: use cudaMemAdvise/CUDAMEMSET_RANGE on supported runtimes or a lightweight reference count + pinned flag for other backends
Batch alignment: attach batch_id to outstanding KV reads; lease duration_hint = max(batch_remaining_ms * 1.2, min_pin_ms) to cover jitter
Preemption behavior: allocator must support transient pin windows that do not block OOM fallback path. If OOM imminent, pinned pages are demoted rather than dropped to avoid costly thrashing
Backpressure: coordinator will reduce prefetch concurrency per GPU when resident > X% (configurable), with dynamic X tuned in perf runs
Interaction with continuous batching: pinned pages are prioritized for coalesced IO when merging requests in batch assembler
Compatibility: ensure behavior falls back to previous eviction logic when runtime flag disabled; tests must validate both paths
test_plan: Integration test: synthetic batcher + prefetcher run on single GPU profile comparing eviction counts with/without pinning
Perf harness: 10-minute sustained mixed workload (60% short-chat, 40% long-context) measuring P50/P90/P95 and GPU memory churn
Chaos test: forced OOM while pinned pages exist to confirm demotion strategy keeps runtime healthy
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag kv.lease_pinning=false by default
Canary: enable on dedicated pool with non-production tenant traffic for 48h
Ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% across dedicated pools if metrics meet thresholds
Fallback: remote toggle to disable lease pinning and trigger immediate graceful demotion of pinned pages

updates: 2026-02-21: Design sync held with Runtime and Batching teams. Decided on advisory lease rather than hard lock to preserve OOM paths.
2026-02-26: Prototype API checked in (PR #4128). Unit tests passing on linux-gpu CI. Initial microbench shows 18% lower eviction attempts for synthetic trace.

2026-03-01: Integrated pin/unpin into batch assembler (PR #4189). Observed a 4% P95 increase in a long-tail chat benchmark when pinning entire 512-token pages; added heuristic to limit pin duration based on token horizon.
2026-03-03: Infra provided driver shim guidance; on-prem images need libcudart >= 11.7 for memadvise path. Added fallback to software reference counting.
2026-03-05: Ran 10-minute mixed workload perf harness. Eviction rate down 34% and P95 latency within 3% of baseline using tuned duration_hint. Preparing canary checklist.
